pages.title: Preface
pages.preview: A reasoner can predict a device’s display without knowing how it relates to the physical state. It can find a successful repair without retaining the evidence needed to justify it. It can store a correct proof whose premises no longer describe the system on which it is about to act. This book asks what a representation must retain for knowledge to remain usable.

pages.preview: The mathematical question is not whether one machine can store an account of its environment. It is whether the account supports the questions, operations, corrections, and changes of representation to which the machine is committed. A description can be internally consistent and still fail to determine the information its consumer requires. It can encode an exact local state while being incompatible with another view of the same purported object. Conversely, a coarse representation can discard most of the ambient variables and preserve every continuation relevant to a declared task.

pages.preview: Relationality is always assessed relative to a way of dividing a realization into components. That dependence is not a minor technicality. If every participant, artifact, and channel is merged into one component, the complete workspace becomes local by definition. pages.preview: The word society is easily applied to a collection of agents that exchange messages. That usage conceals distinctions important to both mathematics and social theory. A cluster of predictors controlled by one scheduler may act as a coherent unit while having no independent decision centers. A set of autonomous services may compete for resources yet lack shared institutions. Conversely, a population may sustain institutions, disagreements, and an archive of precedents while possessing no coherent global policy. None of these arrangements is contradictory. They occupy different parts of the space of possible organizations.

pages.preview: Permissions describe available actions; obligations constrain continuations. The debt created by an urgency exchange is not satisfied merely because the creditor remains authorized to ask for service. It requires a particular future event. A finite obligation record can be written as \[o=(\mathsf{id},i,j,\varphi,d,\mathsf{authority},\mathsf{status}),\] where \(i\) and \(j\) are the debtor and beneficiary offices, \(\varphi\) specifies a fulfillment event, and \(d\) is a deadline under an agreed clock. Status distinguishes pending, fulfilled, breached, and validly discharged obligations. Cancellation must itself satisfy the declared authorization rule; deleting a record is not fulfillment.

pages.preview: An institution can continue to operate while becoming less answerable to the parties it affects. It can preserve a rule whose authority has expired, fund sanctions but not appeals, or treat unfinished obligations as a reason never to accept an authorized ending. None of these possibilities is excluded by persistence alone. The remaining question is therefore not simply whether a computational organization survives. It is whether the same realized organization respects the limits of its authority, supports effective correction, and can enter a specified suspension or settlement state.

pages.preview: Let \(q:X_{\mathrm f}\to X_{\mathrm f}/\operatorname{Ker}C\) be the canonical quotient map. Since \(C\) is surjective, there is a unique vector-space isomorphism \[\widetilde C:X_{\mathrm f}/\operatorname{Ker}C\to X_{\mathrm c},\qquad C=\widetilde Cq.\] The multilinear map \(CA_m^{\mathrm f}:X_{\mathrm f}^m\to X_{\mathrm c}\) descends if and only if its value is unchanged when one input is altered by an element of \(\operatorname{Ker}C\). The induced quotient tensor has the coarse space as its target: \[\overline A_m:(X_{\mathrm f}/\operatorname{Ker}C)^m\longrightarrow X_{\mathrm c},\qquad \overline A_m([x_1],\ldots,[x_m])=CA_m^{\mathrm f}(x_1,\ldots,x_m).\] It follows that \[A_m^{\mathrm c}=\overline A_m(\widetilde C^{-1},\ldots,\widetilde C^{-1}).\] There is no additional output factor \(\widetilde C\) in this convention, since \(\overline A_m\) already takes values in \(X_{\mathrm c}\). Equivalently, define the quotient-valued tensor \[\overline B_m([x_1],\ldots,[x_m])=qA_m^{\mathrm f}(x_1,\ldots,x_m).\] The slot-kernel criterion makes this independent of the representatives. Now \(\overline A_m=\widetilde C\overline B_m\), and the alternative correctly typed formula is \[A_m^{\mathrm c}=\widetilde C\overline B_m(\widetilde C^{-1},\ldots,\widetilde C^{-1}).\] This formulation makes Theorem PRIQ.3.1 independent of coordinates and of the chosen right inverse.
